title: Rate Department Table: Winter Retention Months at the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
At the anniversary cash-out of a Net Energy Metering agreement, retention months are held in the bank when the winter bills of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system make up a large part of the year's offsettable charges.

**Winter share.** The energy plus Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of the hosting service agreement's winter-season bills dated in the 12 months before the cash-out, divided by those charges of all its bills dated in those months, rounded to four decimals.

**Rule.** When the winter share is at least the high winter share of 0.60, there are the high retention months of 2. When it is at least the mid winter share of 0.40 but below 0.60, there is the mid retention month count of 1. Below 0.40 no retention months are held.

**Records read.** For each bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement dated in the 12 months before the cash-out: its pricing season (summer or winter), its energy charge and its Power Supply Cost Recovery charge.

## Retention months

| Winter share | Retention months |
|---|---|
| 0.6000 or more | 2 |
| 0.4000 to 0.5999 | 1 |
| Below 0.4000 | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

- Winter-season bills with energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of 712.40, out of 1180.00 for all bills of the 12 months: 712.40 divided by 1180.00 is 0.60373, rounded to 0.6037, so 2 retention months.
- Winter charges of 590.00 out of 1180.00: a share of 0.5000, so 1 retention month.
- Winter charges of 469.90 out of 1180.00: 0.39822, rounded to 0.3982, so none.
